title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：toast　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 toast 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1995 the baker ① made the toast that no customer in the bakery would have recorded, and he said the making was the whole of the week. The ② toast, meaning the bread itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a toast, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ toast in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ toast at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A toast, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the baker said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the toast was the whole of the matter, meaning the cheer and not the bread. The ⑥ toast, meaning the cheer and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; toast, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a bread and a cheer. He said the cheer is the part they remember.

By 2000 the ⑦ toast had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ toast of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of recording; toast, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ toast I remember is the bread recorded in the bill, which closed in 2002 and is still recorded as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ toast, my mother said in 2004, is the only bread that improves by being recorded; every toast, she said, is a cheer that has agreed to look like a bread. She said the cheer was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 烤面包；祝酒（指糕饼铺里每一片旁边的那一片）
B. n. 烤面包；祝酒（指那片烤面包本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the toast 烤这一片烤面包
D. n. 烤面包；祝酒（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 烤面包之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的烤面包之事）
F. n. 烤面包；祝酒（指账单里写到、被记载的那一片）
G. n. 烤面包、庆贺（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 庆贺（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: make the toast 意为“烤这一片烤面包”，1995 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯记载的一片烤面包做了一遍。
toast 意为“烤面包；祝酒”，指那片烤面包本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记载。
toast 意为“烤面包；祝酒”，指糕饼铺里每一片旁边的那一片，每一片旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
toast 意为“烤面包；祝酒”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
toast 意为“烤面包、庆贺”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这片庆贺就是那件事的全部。
toast 意为“庆贺”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那片烤面包，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
toast 意为“烤面包；祝酒”，指账单里写到、被记载的那一片，到 2000 年这一片成了账单里的一行。
toast 意为“烤面包之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的烤面包之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的记载。
toast 意为“烤面包；祝酒”，我记得的是账单里记载过的那一片，2002 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一片。
toast 为抽象总称，母亲 2004 年说，烤面包是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的烤面包。
